input: n is an integer in [0, 20]. Integers are plain int, excluding bool; lists and strings are ordinary list/str values, not subclasses. No concurrent mutation, getters or modified standard built-ins are allowed. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Declared size bounds are not a guarantee of available memory or completion within an unqualified runtime budget.
return: A fresh list of 2^n integers giving the binary-reflected n-bit Gray code, beginning at zero. All integers from zero through 2^n - 1 occur once; adjacent codes differ in one bit, including last-to-first for n >= 1. n = 0 returns [0], with no one-bit cyclic-adjacency claim for its self-edge. The exact reflected ordering agrees between both candidates.
mutation_aliasing: No mutable input exists. The result is a new container per call. New values are appended by reading the previously present prefix backward; there is no external array or shared mutable state.
numeric: At each stage, bit is the next power of two above all existing codes, so bit + code sets that new bit without bitwise coercion. All codes and the final bit are at most 2^20 = 1048576, exact safe integers. The output length is at most 1048576.
complexity: Theta(2^n) time and output space, with O(1) auxiliary state excluding output. Reflections are read directly backward from the original prefix rather than allocating a reversed copy. The initial loop index is captured before appending, so a stage exactly doubles its prior code count.
